EPEVER — Remote Meter User Manual MT50, V3.5 (2021-06) — downloaded and committed this session at docs/epever-mt50-manual-v3.5.pdf, source https://www.epever.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/MT50-Manual-EN-V3.5.pdf

EPEVER MT50 download page https://www.epever.com/download/mt50-remote-meter-download/ — lists exactly one document, MT50-Manual-EN-V3.3.pdf. No communication/protocol document is offered for the MT50.

transport: RS-485 over RJ45 · the MT50 is the bus MASTER polling the controller, not an addressable slave · baud rate NOT stated in either MT50 manual · no slave ID · pins 1,2 = +5~12 V power input (drawn from the controller), 3,4 = RS485-B, 5,6 = RS485-A, 7,8 = GND
refutedOnReview: REFUTED on every leg. The dialect should not exist.  1. The `vendor-doc` tag has nothing behind it — and the claim admits it. The source list itself states "No communication/protocol document is offered for the MT50," which is self-refuting for a `vendor-doc` confidence tag. Per the skill's own legend (docs/catalog/README.md:79), `vendor-doc` means "from the manufacturer's own protocol document." No such document is
gotchas: THIS IS NOT A DIALECT AND CANNOT HAVE A DRIVER. Neither MT50 manual (V2.1 or V3.5) contains a single register address, baud rate, or slave ID, and EPEVER's own MT50 download page offers no protocol document — only the user manual. The MT50 is a display that polls the controller; nothing on the bus can read the MT50. Re

The retailer framing that put the MT50 in a battery-monitor survey is wrong. It measures nothing. Every number on its screen is read out of the charge controller, so the truthful way to get those numbers is the epever-tracer-a map over the same wire — the MT50 is a second consumer of that data, not a source.

It is a second Modbus MASTER on the meter bus. RS-485 assumes one master; an MT50 left plugged in while the gateway polls will collide. This repo already records the same finding (docs/DEVICES.md:111, docs/INVENTORY.md:198). Tolerate retries or unplug it.

V3.5 §1.3 note: 'Please use the communication plug, marked with "MT," to connect MT50.' On controllers with separate MT and PC ports, the MT50 has its own port — which is why an MT50 and a gateway do not automatically share one bus segment, and why the collision only bites when they are bridged.

CONTRADICTION between the two vendor manuals on which controllers it fits. V2.1 (the copy already committed) lists only LSxxxxB(P), VSxxxxBN, TracerxxxxBN(P) — the XTRA series is absent. V3.5 §1.3 adds iTracer-AD/ND (3.81-4P interface), Tracer-BP (waterproof RS-485 port), and 'Tracer-AN (10A~40A), TRIRON, XTRA' on RJ45
unmappedReports: battery max voltage today / min voltage today (MT50 monitoring page 'Max. Vol' / 'Min. Vol') — no MetricKind, discharge (DC load) energy day / month / total ('DisCh. Energy') — MetricKind has pv-energy-today/total and ac-energy-today/total, but nothing for the DC load output and nothing monthly, charge energy month ('Char. Energy Mon:') — pv-energy-today and pv-energy-total exist, no monthly bucket, controller internal temperature ('Controller Temp.') — `temperature` is documented as ambient; there is no device-temperature MetricKind (same gap already noted for 0x3111 in the epever-tracer-a entry), battery status: Normal / Under voltage / Over discharge — no MetricKind and no ValueKind for it (ValueKind covers ChargeStage, RunState, Weather only), PV connection status Connect / DisConnect, and the per-subsystem fault flags (battery / PV / load / controller 'Fault: No') — no MetricKind, load working mode (Manual / Light On-Off / Light On+Timer / Time Control) — no MetricKind to report it and no CommandKind to set it (CommandKind stops at set-switch, start-generator, stop-generator, clear-fault, set-charge-current-limit, start-equalize, mark-refuelled, reset-counter, identify), DeviceKind gap, not a metric gap: the MT50 is a display/HMI. DeviceKind has no such variant, and `battery-monitor` is the wrong one — it measures nothing.
